add.content: A flat prior makes new PSD peaks arise from measurement rather than assumed distribution shape.
add.evidence_span: An uninformative flat prior for conveys no information about the form of the distribution; expecting a flat PSD at the outset means that new information (peaks) in comes only from the measurement.

add.content: Bayesian MaxEnt lets measurement uncertainty determine the regularization weight.
add.evidence_span: Instead, the data and measurement error inherently dictate λ.

add.content: Combined scattering reveals grain structure plus two precipitate-size populations.
add.evidence_span: The combined USAXS–SAXS data after heat treatment suggest the presence of three length scale regimes, namely a low- q power law region for the grain structure of the metal and two precipitate size distributions:

add.content: A new high-q precipitate population grows during heat treatment.
add.evidence_span: The high- q region shows growth of a new first PSD, consistent with precipitation hardening in Ni alloys.

add.content: Conventional inversion can fail when low-q background is nonflat or interparticle effects matter.
add.evidence_span: Conventional inverse transformation using equation (2) gives misleading results in the absence of flat at low q

add.content: Grain scattering, a second PSD, and structure-factor effects complicate MaxEnt inference.
add.evidence_span: The presence of the grain structure, second PSD and structure factor together makes implementation of MaxEnt difficult

add.content: The TIDC model broadens LSW distributions with an additional shape parameter.
add.evidence_span: For example, Ardell & Ozolins (2005 [2] ) developed the TIDC model of precipitation hardening, defining a PSD that incorporates a shape parameter in addition to a characteristic radius .

add.content: Avoiding assumed PSD forms motivated the MaxEnt approach.
add.evidence_span: The desire to avoid prior assumptions about the form of the PSD solution drove the development of MaxEnt approaches that seek the best explanation for the PSD given only the measured data and the shape of the precipitates.

add.content: In situ scattering follows PSD evolution continuously in one heated specimen.
add.evidence_span: In situ X-ray or neutron scattering provides an alternative method for PSD study using sequential measurements on a single sample undergoing heat treatment.

add.content: PSD mode, inferred diameter, and superlattice growth follow similar temporal trajectories.
add.evidence_span: Plotting these three parameters on the same time axis demonstrates that all three follow similar trajectories.
